The new entry is, of course, “Black Panther,” which is set to surpass Paramount’s “Titanic.”
At the beginning of the weekend “Titanic” had posted an all-time domestic gross of $659.36 million while “Black Panther” had chalked up $659.26 million in domestic ticket sales. That the new film will supplant number 2 all-time — Fox’s “Avatar”— is doubtful. The 2009 blockbuster is ahead by about $100 million.
The entire movie industry should be giving thanks to the “Black Panther.” According to Boxofficemojo.com, domestic ticket sales in March were down 24% year over year and full quarter ticket sales were down 2%. “Black Panther” is the difference. Yet some companies still had bad news that sent their shares lower. Michael Kors Holdings (NYSE:KORS), Chico’s FAS (NYSE:CHS), and Daktronics (NASDAQ:DAKT) were among the worst performers on the day. Here’s why they did so poorly. [By Shane Hupp]
Media stories about Daktronics (NASDAQ:DAKT) have trended somewhat positive this week, according to Accern Sentiment. Accern identifies negative and positive media coverage by analyzing more than 20 million blog and news sources in real time. Accern ranks coverage of public companies on a scale of negative one to one, with scores nearest to one being the most favorable. Daktronics earned a daily sentiment score of 0.11 on Accern’s scale.
